hero.headline: Indian River County responds to 93% waste management fee spike for Vero Beach condos
hero.body:
Indian River County officials have addressed concerns from condominium owners in Vero Beach following a significant increase in waste management fees under a new contract with Waste Management that began in October 2025. The monthly fees for condo associations jumped from $11 to $21, representing a roughly 93% increase that has prompted complaints from residents.

Thomas Clark raised his concerns during a WPTV Let's Hear It event in Vero Beach, speaking with WPTV Anchor Mike Trim about the spike in his monthly condo association bill. Clark expressed dissatisfaction with the increase and suggested the county should provide assistance to residents if the contract terms resulted from a county error. WPTV brought these concerns directly to the Indian River County Department of Utility Services during a video conference meeting to investigate the matter.

County officials explained that the new contract includes additional benefits for condo residents that were not available previously. Himanshu Mehta of the Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District said residents can now place bulk items near condo dumpsters, a service the previous contract did not offer. Mehta and other county officials pointed out that the contract was approved during public hearings held in 2024, emphasizing the importance of community participation in such proceedings.

Mehta offered to provide more detailed explanations to concerned residents and their homeowner associations. He indicated that he and his team are available to attend HOA meetings to walk through the process and answer questions about the fee increase and new services. Residents seeking additional information can find updates on Indian River County public hearings on the county website, where current recycling and garbage schedules are also available. The county stressed that community involvement in public hearings remains crucial for residents who want to stay informed about decisions affecting their waste management services and associated costs.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher killed in St. Lucie County shooting, suspect identified
cards.body:
A 66-year-old Fort Pierce man was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive in St. Lucie County. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office identified the victim as Andre Leonard Barnes, an art teacher for St. Lucie Public Schools. Deputies responded to the home around 3:30 p.m. Tuesday after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot Barnes with a rifle. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office identified the suspect as Dale A. Mincey. Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. The sheriff's office has not yet filed additional charges related to the fatal shooting as the investigation continues.

St. Lucie Public Schools released a statement following Barnes' death. The district acknowledged the loss of the art teacher, though the full statement was not included in available reports. Barnes had been working as an educator in the St. Lucie County school system at the time of his death.

The sheriff's office said the homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. Deputies said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public. Additional information will be released as it becomes available.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County offers free rip current safety training at three pools this summer
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation is hosting three free rip current safety demonstrations using a new simulation machine at local public pools. The training teaches proper escape techniques in a controlled environment.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three free rip current safety demonstrations this summer using a new rip current simulation machine that creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies. The demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love. According to the National Weather Service, there have been 23 rip current fatalities this year so far in the United States.

The county has scheduled three sessions. The first is July 19 from 1 to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. The second is July 28 from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event with no registration required on a first-come, first-served basis. The third is August 16 from 1 to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. The proper technique to escape a rip current is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle.

The roughly 93% increase prompted Vero Beach resident Thomas Clark to raise concerns during a WPTV Let's Hear It community meetup with anchor Mike Trim.

"It's certainly something I'm available for — my team is available to provide that." Residents can stay updated on Indian River County public hearings and find current recycling and garbage schedules on the county website.

cards.headline: Jensen Beach Park restrooms and Sea Turtle Beach Cafe rebuild expected by late 2027
cards.teaser: Beachgoers at Jensen Beach Park are waiting for the rebuild of restrooms and a concession building destroyed in a fire on New Year's Eve in December 2024. The county says final funding is expected to be approved in September.
cards.body:
Jensen Beach Park restrooms and the Sea Turtle Beach Cafe are being rebuilt after a fire destroyed the facilities on New Year's Eve in December 2024. Kevin Abbate, the Parks and Recreation director for Martin County, said the permitting process takes time because the building sits on a protected dune and must go through the Department of Environmental Protection. The design for the new 9,000 square foot Sea Turtle Beach Cafe is 80% complete. The new facility will be about 15 feet in elevation with 100 seats and 33 seats at the bar. Final funding is expected to be approved in September.

The county hopes to start construction in early 2027 with a completion goal of late 2027, just in time for the winter season. The county does not have plans for additional temporary restrooms or facilities. Gonda Ghebert, who contacted WPTV, wrote that beachgoers are left with only one very small restroom facility to serve the entire beach and feels it has become increasingly unreasonable during weekends, holidays, and peak tourist season. Julie Goings, who frequents the beach, said she misses the nice, clean facility with showers and being able to get a snack or drink after leaving the deck.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Clerk's website redirected for hours after third-party service failure
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday, redirecting visitors to another site before coming back online around 1:30 p.m. Clerk and Comptroller Michelle Miller posted a video on social media Tuesday afternoon addressing the outage, assuring the public that no personal or confidential information was compromised or at risk. The clerk's office does not store sensitive personal information on the public-facing website. Miller said the website faced a temporary redirection issue caused by a third-party service provider.

IT Director Jose Clavijo said the office received a report just before 8 a.m. that something was wrong with the county clerk's homepage. Clavijo told reporters that fixing the issue was the absolute highest priority. As soon as he identified the problem, he ordered the service turned off immediately before starting an investigation into what caused the redirection.

When asked if the incident involved any suspicious activity such as a hack, the clerk's office communications team said this was not a hack because no personal information was compromised. Residents could still access information and services on the website through direct links instead of using the homepage. Clavijo said payments, property fraud services, and all other services remained available during the outage. He explained that the main page was the only part of the website affected by the issue.

Clavijo said the office is working to prevent similar issues from happening again. He said that as soon as they identify the exact issue, there will be a tremendous remediation. The office has not provided additional details about which third-party service provider was responsible for the temporary redirection or what specifically caused the malfunction that led to the hours-long outage.

hero.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team nicknames and logos ahead of August debut
hero.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The other two teams are the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters.

The WPBL's debut season begins on Aug. 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. Whitmore told The Associated Press at a scrimmage in March that this is just every little girl's dream to play professional baseball, and now for us to actually be with each other there's so much freedom and peace within it. The league has been years in the making and hopes to create a space for women's baseball players similar to the one the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League did 70 years ago.

Each team identity and name holds a unique meaning tied to notable women in history. The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist.

The team logos reflect their namesakes and identities. The New York Heights logo includes graphic lines surrounding a baseball, mimicking the speed of a fastball and resembling the New York skyline. The San Francisco Firebells logo fuses a bell with a phoenix. The Los Angeles Queens logo is a capital Q topped with four baseball diamonds. The Boston Hunters logo is an osprey, clasping a baseball bat in its talons. With the teams now set and identities established, the league is ready to launch its historic first season in August.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi leads Argentina to 3-2 comeback over Egypt to reach World Cup quarterfinals
cards.teaser: Argentina rallied from a 2-0 deficit in the final 11 minutes to defeat Egypt 3-2 on Tuesday, with Lionel Messi scoring his eighth goal of the tournament.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi scored his record-extending 21st goal at the World Cup in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2 after Argentina trailed by two goals with only 11 minutes of regulation time remaining. Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time to complete the comeback, while Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute. The 39-year-old Messi, who was in tears after the final whistle, scored his eighth goal of the tournament in the 3-2 victory over Egypt on Tuesday. Argentina had trailed 2-0 on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico. The defending champions will next face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri.

Messi missed a chance in the first half when his penalty kick was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir. He later hit the post when the score was 1-0. Despite being the all-time leading scorer at World Cups, Messi has now missed four of eight penalty kicks at the tournament, including one against Austria in the group stage. Egypt took a surprising lead in the 15th minute when Ibrahim got ahead of Lisandro Martinez to meet Marwan Attia's cross and head the ball into the bottom corner. Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962.

cards.headline: United States eliminated from World Cup in 4-1 loss to Belgium
cards.teaser: The United States hopes for a deep World Cup run at home ended when Belgium defeated the Americans 4-1 on Monday night in Seattle.
cards.body:
Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal, helping Belgium expose the Americans' defensive liabilities in a 4-1 win Monday night that earned a quarterfinal berth. While the U.S. was boosted by the presence of star forward Folarin Balogun, whose one-game red-card suspension was controversially lifted by FIFA, American defenders were at fault in a pair of first-half goals and goalkeeper Matt Freese's gaffe gave the Red Devils a third early in the second half. Second-half substitute Romelu Lukaku added Belgium's final goal in the third minute of stoppage time. De Ketelaere put Belgium ahead in the eighth minute, the first time in this year's World Cup the U.S. conceded first.

Malik Tillman tied the score 1-1 in the 31st minute with his second free kick goal of the tournament, but the Americans conceded just 61 seconds after the ensuing kickoff. Coach Mauricio Pochettino showed his frustration by kicking a rack in front of the bench, sending four water bottles flying. American star Christian Pulisic could only watch from the bench after injuring his right foot when he hit a boot of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans on a 52nd-minute shot attempt. Pulisic favored his foot after that and was replaced seven minutes later. After winning three games in a World Cup for the first time in this expanded 48-nation tournament, the U.S. failed in its quest to reach the quarterfinals for the first time since 2002 and lost to Belgium for the seventh straight time since a victory at the initial tournament in 1930.

cards.headline: US-Belgium World Cup match draws record 30 million viewers on Fox
cards.teaser: Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, Fox Sports reported.
cards.body:
Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, Fox Sports reported. According to Fox, the match drew more than 30 million viewers. Viewership peaked at 36 million early in the second half of Monday's match. The United States lost 4-1 to Belgium. Meanwhile, Telemundo said its Spanish-language broadcast reached 12 million viewers, which NBCUniversal said is a record for a U.S. men's national team broadcast. Interest in Monday's match intensified after FIFA announced that Folarin Balogun would be eligible to play against Belgium despite receiving a red card last week against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States' match against Bosnia and Herzegovina also set records. Fox said about 26.4 million viewers tuned in, setting what was then the record for an English-language soccer broadcast in the United States. Telemundo said it drew 9.8 million viewers, the largest Spanish-language audience for a U.S. men's national team match. Fox said its World Cup broadcasts have generated significant interest beyond U.S. matches. The network said last week's Portugal-Croatia match drew more than 11 million viewers, making it the most-watched World Cup match on Fox that did not involve the United States or a final. Fox also said its Mexico-Ecuador broadcast last week drew more than 10 million viewers. Meanwhile, Telemundo said its Mexico-England broadcast delivered 23.1 million viewers.

cards.headline: IOC ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 LA Olympics
cards.teaser: The IOC advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
cards.body:
The move was expected since the International Olympic Committee advised two months ago that athletes from Belarus, Russia's military ally in the full military invasion of Ukraine, should be allowed again to compete with their full national identity. The IOC eased entry requirements to its own events for Russian athletes and teams while provisionally lifting its suspension since October 2023 of the Russian Olympic Committee. The terms of that suspension, imposed when the Russian Olympic body incorporated regional sports councils from occupied regions of Ukraine, no longer applied, the IOC said.

Just 32 athletes from Russia and Belarus competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics as approved neutrals, and combined to win five medals. The Russian team had more than 300 athletes at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics and won 71 medals. The IOC did not yet approve letting Russian athletes and teams compete with their flag and anthem. That decision will come at an appropriate time, it said. The next Olympic competition is the 2026 Youth Summer Games in Dakar, Senegal opening Oct. 31. The IOC said Russian athletes must give multiple doping controls and be part of a recognized testing program to address the lack of confidence in the global sporting community relating to the return of Russian athletes to international competition. The IOC said it will continue to not organize IOC events in Russia or invite Russian government or state officials to its events.

hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc.

The annual festival brings seafood vendors, entertainment, and activities to Indian River County each year. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. organizes the event, which has become a regular fall attraction in Vero Beach.

The festival typically features fresh seafood from regional vendors, live music, and family-friendly entertainment. Previous years have drawn thousands of visitors to the oceanfront community for the multi-day event.

Specific dates, venue location, and vendor information for the November 2026 festival have not yet been announced by organizers. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. released the initial announcement on Monday.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County offers free rip current safety training at three public pools this summer
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three free sessions using a new rip current simulation machine to teach residents and visitors proper escape techniques in controlled pool environments.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County residents and visitors can learn life-saving skills this summer through free rip current safety demonstrations at local public pools. The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using their new rip current simulation machine, which creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. The hands-on training aims to build swimmer confidence and prepare participants for real ocean conditions before they head to area beaches.

"Education is one of the most effective tools we have to prevent water-related emergencies," said Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager. "These demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love."

The county has scheduled three free demonstrations this summer. The first is July 19 from 1 to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool, with registration required and limited to 50 participants. The second is July 28 from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event, with no registration required and first-come, first-served. The third is August 16 from 1 to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool, with registration required and limited to 50 participants.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water that flow away from shore, capable of quickly pulling swimmers away from the beach. According to the National Weather Service, there have been 23 rip current fatalities this year so far in the United States. Many swimmers make a critical mistake when caught in a rip current by trying to swim directly back to shore, which often leads to dangerous exhaustion. The proper technique is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle. For more information about the rip current safety demonstrations, contact St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation.

Indian River County condo owners saw their monthly waste management fees nearly double from $11 to $21 under a new Waste Management contract that began in October 2025. The roughly 93% increase prompted Vero Beach resident Thomas Clark to raise concerns during a WPTV Let's Hear It community meetup with anchor Mike Trim.

WPTV brought Clark's concerns directly to the Indian River County Department of Utility Services during a video conference meeting. County officials explained the increase stems from the new contract with Waste Management that was approved during 2024 public hearings. Clark expressed his dissatisfaction with the situation, telling Trim he was not happy with the increase and questioned who should bear the financial burden. "I understand that if the county made a mistake, it should be on their end, you would think," Clark said. "Maybe look at something to help us out."

However, county officials say condo residents are receiving additional benefits under the new contract. Himanshu Mehta of the Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District explained that residents can now place bulk items near condo dumpsters, a service that was not previously available. Mehta and other county officials emphasized the importance of community involvement in public hearings where such contracts are approved, noting this particular contract went through the approval process during 2024 hearings.

Mehta offered to provide more detailed explanations to homeowner associations concerned about the changes. "If this gentleman wanted to invite us or his HOA wanted to invite us to a meeting, we're happy to send someone to go over this process in more detail," Mehta said. "It's certainly something I'm available for — my team is available to provide that." Residents can stay updated on Indian River County public hearings and find current recycling and garbage schedules on the county website.
